components.name: Emergency safeguard
components.headline: recall 1.000 on 19 emergencies in 308 test lines
inputs: free text from the bot, the form, or a crew note
components.model: weighted lexicon + immobility patch, plus a TF-IDF classifier at 0.45

gates.gate: zero false alarms on hydrant / fire escape / fire lane
works with no model loaded (fails closed)
gates.measured: rules run in process; a failure shows the 911 advisory

components.name: NLP intake bot
components.headline: macro-F1 0.858 across 308 hand-written messages
components.model: MiniLM embeddings + logistic regression, trained on the realistic-prior variant

gates.gate: out-of-scope messages never silently routed to a crew
under 200 ms per message on CPU
slot span F1 >= 0.60 on the location and time slots, measured on messages labelled by hand
the shipped slot filler beats the pattern baseline, with the two confidence intervals not overlapping
gates.measured: tagger low end 0.641 above baseline high end 0.543

components.name: Credibility and escalation
components.headline: ranks citizens at Spearman 0.91 against their hidden honesty
inputs: their past confirmed outcomes with request types
closures at the same place and type
components.model: decaying Beta, 180-day half-life, centred on the confirmation rate expected for the request types that citizen actually reports
components.notes: The original gate asked for mean error under 10 points against hidden honesty. That gate was wrong and has been replaced. The two are on different scales: in this data a citizen with honesty 0.9 can only ever reach a 0.73 confirmation rate, because genuine reports are still closed as nothing-found about 16% of the time. Ranking and fairness are what this score has to get right.

gates.gate: a new citizen starts at exactly neutral 50
one bad report never drops a trusted citizen into the LOW band
ranks citizens correctly, Spearman >= 0.85 for 10+ reports
reporting hard-to-confirm problems costs under 2 points at equal honesty
gates.measured: 0.3 points (it was 4.0 before the base-rate correction)

components.name: Predictive alerting
components.headline: catches 87% of real water and sewer spikes on storm days
outputs: alerts: borough, family, expected vs baseline, lift, severity, drivers
components.model: gradient boosting with a Poisson loss, beating the no-weather baseline and a Poisson GLM

examples: Queens 30 Oct: 67 mm, 699 reports against 83 normal, warned
Bronx 06 Jul: 61 mm, 215 reports against 55 normal, warned
Manhattan 29 Jul: 59 mm, 59 reports against 35 normal, warned

gates.gate: beats the no-weather baseline on count error
catches at least 70% of real spikes on storm days
a failure shows as failed, never as a quiet day
